utterances.text: And when these mines which they shot at were activated, was anyone injured?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he didn't state that they shot at the mines. I believe that the shooting activated the mines. That's a point for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As far as you know were the Serbs deliberately targeting the mines? Were they shooting at them to activate them or was it accidental?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs knew where they had placed the mines, and when the mines were activated -- I mean before, when people were killed. And since they knew where the mines were, they were shooting at the other mines as well in order to activate them, I mean all the other mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And when they did that and the mines activated, was anyone injured?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one was injured in my group. People dispersed. I mean, this group was broken up, and there was a lot of shooting from machine-guns, PAMs, from the village of Radijevici. And we had no chance at all to enter the village of Radijevici because we were already afraid of the mines. Maybe we thought there were more mines. And so the group was broken up completely and the people dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that four soldiers were killed on those -- by stepping on the mines. Is that correct, that the four people who were killed --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were they all men, all the people who were killed stepping on the mines?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a nurse in that group of four people who were killed. And as I heard later on I think she was from either the village of Tokolavci [phoen] or Radovcici, something like that. I can't remember at the moment which village exactly, but maybe Tokoljac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the men who were killed, do you know if they were in uniform or not?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the men had no uniforms at all and two people were killed at the same time and -- or rather, two people were -- the bodies were taken away and two bodies remained. Perhaps there was nobody to take them away. And so together with another guy who was also unarmed, I set out in the direction of Zanjevo and we came across a mine, and this guy tripped over a mine. But fortunately, the mine was attached to a branch, and he tripped over and the branch started swaying and I managed to draw his attention to the fact that there was a mine. And so he stopped and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you but I need to break it down, and I'm going to come back to that in a moment. But I first want to show you Exhibit D740, please, with the assistance of the usher. And before we leave Radijevici you said: "And we had no chance at all to enter the village of Radijevici." And I want you to look at this document, and it's from the Bratunac garrison command, strictly confidential, number 24312, dated 6th October, 1992, to the Birac Brigade command. And for the moment I'm going to just go to the second paragraph. "Our forces are holding Radijevici village but other villages, Fakovici, Boljevici, and Grabovacka Rijeka are empty." Now, does that correspond with what you were telling us now in your information that in fact no one actually entered, no Muslims entered, Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've finished with that exhibit for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were any Muslims, to your knowledge, killed by Serbs who were shooting from these houses in Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment when we set out towards Abdulici and Zanjevo, I started describing the situation and the fact that we did -- disactivated that mine and we continued towards Zanjevo. And together with this neighbour of mine, I managed to get through a part of that creek where Serb soldiers noticed us and they started shooting at us. At any rate, we managed to enter the village of Zanjevo itself. Upon our arrival in the village -- when we arrived, two people were hit by bullets coming from Radijevici, and I rushed to assist them, but it was too late. They were mortally wounded, and there was no chance whatsoever of any assistance being provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. So you've mentioned two people in any event who were killed by shooting from Radijevici. One thing you mentioned earlier which I want to go back to, you said how your friend or another man nearly triggered a mine but it didn't go off. Did you do anything with that -- with that mine which didn't actually activate?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I deactivated that mine. I detached from that rope that was attached to both the tree and the mine. And I disassembled it. And I put it in this guy's backpack, so we carried it with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So this person was wearing a rucksack. Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. That was the problem we were familiar with. I'll repeat the question. Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage you're in Zanjevo. At this time were there any civilians in the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zanjevo itself where those two people were killed, there were hundreds of civilians with horses, backpacks, sacks, and the shelling that was coming from the direction of Fakovici was accompanied by shooting from the village of Radijevici. And so the entire area was under threat, and the houses had been burnt beforehand. So there was no means of survival there. And I myself asked people who had horses to give me a horse or two so that I could carry the dead bodies and take them to a house that was not completely burnt down in order to prevent the bodies being shot to pieces by those shells. And the answer I got from these people is, They're already dead. There's nothing to preserve anymore, and we must load food that we had come for in order to feed our children who are starving and they are thirsty and they don't have any clothes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say that "the houses had been burnt beforehand," these are houses in which village?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And who, to your knowledge, had burnt those houses?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, it was done by the Serbs, the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to shelling from Fakovici. Can you tell us what sort of calibre, what sort of artillery was shooting from Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are mortars from Fakovici that were shelling Zanjevo at that time. And later on when we carried those dead bodies into a house in Zanjevo that had a roof where we could put them, I went in the direction of Zanjevo creek, and there were quite a few civilians in those houses and farms and they were collecting food in the village of Abdulici. And when I managed to get to Radijevici Potok, I spotted a house between Fakovici and Radijevici Potok, the house about which we had known all along, that it had been secured with sandbags and that Serb soldiers from Fakovici were stationed there, and they were using machine-guns and PAM, I believe. And after a short while, the noise died down and -- and so there was no more any shooting coming from that particular house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you a bit about that house. You said "the house about which we had known all along." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our observers, reconnaissance men who moved around the area before this counter-attack at Fakovici, they would go down to the places that I've marked on the map and mentioned in the period of time ranging between July, August, and September. And they would go down to those places. And people who used to go to Zanjevo at night in order to collect food, people who were going hungry, they spotted that house, they noticed it, and they realised that there were shots being fired from that house even at night if they happened to notice our refugees who were going back to collect food.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if subsequently anything was found inside that house?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a later stage, after the end of those events, people from Abdulici who entered that house who -- that went close to that house, well, I heard that Djoko Djokic was killed in that house and that some weapons were found there, the weapons that were used in order to shoot people from that house. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know which -- what weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Machine-guns and automatic weapons and PAMs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned Djoko Djokic. Is that the same Djoko Djokic whom you saw in Joseva in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to what those people from Zanjevo said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown D45, Defence Exhibit 45. And this is a list of killed fighters, VP -- well, it's -- sorry, I'll start from the beginning. VRS, Army of Republika Srpska, list of killed fighters, VP military post, 740 Bratunac from 1992 to 1996. And if you turn to number 16 we see Djoko Djokic, father's name Nedeljko, born 27th of September, 1958, in Boljevici, died in Fakovici on the 5th of October, 1992. Does that correspond with -- well, does the birth date and the father's name appear correct for Djoko Djokic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Djoko Djokic, yes. He is from Radijevici, yes, and that he lived in Fakovici, yes. And also that he was killed on the 5th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I can clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he can perhaps also clarify one thing. He seems to know a lot of information on this house in particular, and one piece of information is that Djoko Djokic was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Inside that house. Was it Djoko Djokic's own house? This is -- or was it someone else's house and Djoko Djokic happened to be there at some point in time when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you help us with that, Mr. Alic.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't Djoko Djokic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, it was a house from a village near Biljeg. The name used to be Mosce. And that man built a house before the war at that spot where it was, because when I was a student at school I already knew that. I think that the name of the village near Mosce is Grubanovici, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It might not be clear. You're saying that it's a man who built that house and the man is from a village near Biljeg?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from Biljeg, from just below Biljeg. The village was Grubanovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And he built the house where Djoko Djokic died. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And at the time that Djoko Djokic died there, do you know was it a residential house or was it some other type of house or being used for some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone used to live in that house, but I do know that it was surrounded by sandbags and that positions, machine-gun positions, could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, I think he can give us more information to be able to identify this house, say the -- since he seems to be very familiar with Fakovici itself --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- whether he knows the name of the street. The reason, I mean, I think it should appear very obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, even on the map if the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he can identify or help us identify this house, name of the street, if he knows it, any neighbouring houses that he can identify to us as belonging to particular individuals. I don't know. He is supposedly receiving interpretation of what I am saying, so he can answer direct without your need to put the question, in other words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this -- there was no street to speak of in Fakovici. I can show you on the map where this house was, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. If you could do that, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I put a different mark there? I indicated it -- I put a cross there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest is that you put another cross on that cross so it will be eight-pointed rather than four-pointed and we can distinguish it from the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It's six-pointed, but it doesn't really make a difference. So the spot where the witness suggests that this house stood on is being shown, marked by him, on the map by means of a star, superimposed on the circle surrounding Fakovici, on the same map, D827, D827.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: On this same subject, Mr. Alic, you mention shooting from houses in Radijevici. I'm not going to ask you, unless it's possible, for you to mark on the map all the houses where shooting was coming from Radijevici, unless you think you can do that. Would you be able to mark all the locations where shooting was coming from houses or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you can, then -- and you're going to mark on -- put marks on the map, put S instead of the usual X.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I first approach it this way, Your Honour, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whichever way because I don't want to interfere. I'm trying to help, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there is one point, though, which is -- it's a matter perhaps I won't discuss in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have a better map of Fakovici and Radijevici close --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We don't personally, Your Honour, and the point -- the point which I -- which think I should make for the record is that we don't propose -- we don't think it's incumbent on us to locate every location where shooting was coming from houses; it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course not. You don't have -- you don't carry any burden in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. As long as that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So Radijevici, if you can tell us how many houses -- from how many houses shooting was coming.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. At that point in time we were still in the forest. There was shooting from every house in that particular area. I can't say now that there was firing coming from 10 or 20 houses, but each house that was there, there was firing, somebody was firing from it, firing at the area in which we happened to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And then moving to Fakovici, you're not saying, are you, that the only shooting on that day came from the house where Djoko Djokic was found, or are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I approached Radijevici-Zanjevski-Potok, I saw the arrival and I saw shooting from that house, from the direction of Fakovici. There was an enormous amount of shooting in Fakovici, too. I didn't go any further from Radijevici Potok in the direction of Fakovici, but there were loud sounds of shooting in the middle of Fakovici itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So you're not saying that the only house from which there was shooting was the house where Djoko Djokic died? Sorry, if you didn't understand, I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just before we leave this map, is it correct -- you made -- Fakovici you made this cross or star at the end of Fakovici toward the direction of Abdulici. Now, was this house we are talking about still in the area of Fakovici where you had other houses around, or was it somehow an isolated house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house was between Zanjevski Potok and Fakovici, meaning there was another small house just next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But it was not in the centre of Fakovici, so to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This house was in Fakovici, though, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's established, Mr. Jones. I mean, we don't need to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. But I will pursue this matter, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was there shooting from other houses besides that house on that day?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the direction of Fakovici there was firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. From the direction of the centre of Fakovici would you say?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the centre of Fakovici, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just going back to D45, we've seen Djoko Djokic there. Now, I want to ask you this: Are you aware of a tradition --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you aware of a tradition in Bosnia where military units are named after their dead commanders?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So, in other words, a person, a commander of a unit, is then killed in action and then the unit is renamed after the fallen commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that. I want to direct you to number 221 where it says "Slavko Jovanovic, born 4 June, 1954," and it says that he died on the 28th of June, 1992, in Bradjevina. Is that the Slavko Jovanovic you testified about seeing in Joseva ordering Serb soldiers to attack, kill, and burn in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then if we go to number 298 and we see the name Ognjen Markovic, born 20 December, 1950, in Fakovici. Apparently he died on the 8th of June, 1992, in Podkorjen. Is that the Ognjen Markovic who you testified about earlier?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know, if Podkorjen a Serb or a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I'd also ask that the witness be shown D732. And for the record, it says "notes and orders of the brigade and 5th Infantry Battalion Fakovici." And the second page, "list of the killed combatants from Fakovici, Boljevici, Tegare area."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll just wait until you have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I ask also if the Defence would just wait a moment because it was not on their exhibit list and we'd like to get our own copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It is not in mine either, actually. I have 735 and 734 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. It was an addition this morning. It is that exhibit there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you're ready, Ms. Sellers, let me know. It's also on the ELMO, although we are not seeing much. Yes, can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll look at the ELMO for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have a spare copy if either Your Honours or the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can follow you on the ELMO, but it's okay. The Prosecution has found it, has located it, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I just direct your attention to names at number 10, Slavko Jovanovic; number 9, Ognjen Markovic; and number 32, Djoko Djokic; and that this document -- and my apologies -- yes, and this document is entitled, as I say, "the notes and orders of the brigade, 5th Infantry Battalion Fakovici." Were you aware, Mr. Alic, of a battalion, a Serb battalion, being based in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I'm going to come back to that, the question of the battalion, but for the time being that's sufficient with this exhibit. Now, we're on the 5th of October, 1992. You've described what you've seen. You've described boats coming from the other side of the Drina. Did you see any activity on the other side of the Drina, in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the shooting from Fakovici ceased, in my recollection this was at 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon, I was still at Radijevici Potok. There was a loud noise of vehicles across the Drina towards Bacevci. A short while later there was heavy artillery fire from the direction of Bacevci and Bacevacko Polje. It was virtually impossible to survive in the area in which I happened to be, so we ran back to the woods. But artillery fire was opened across the Fakovici and Zanjevo area as far as Radijevici. From the last houses in the Muslim village of Zanjevo and across to Fakovici, including the centre of Fakovici, as well as the forests behind Fakovici and above the village of Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So if you can just clarify that last answer. From the last houses in the Muslim village of Zanjevo and across to Fakovici, including the centre of Fakovici, as well as the forest behind Fakovici and above the village of Zanjevo, what? What were you saying about those areas?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This entire area was being shelled from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Including the centre of Fakovici was being --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I want to get your words correct. Yes. That area was being shelled from Serbia. Can you mark on the map, please, where Bacevacko Polje is.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Bacevci. I put a circle around it. This is Bacevacko Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It needs some explanation for the record. The witness encircles the village of Bacevci across the Drina on the Serbian side, and then he appends a tail to that circle which he intends to denote with Bacevacko Polje. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alic, roughly what's the distance from where the artillery was firing in Bacevacko Polje over to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say, but I reckon between one and a half and two kilometres as the crow flies, that at least is my assessment. The distance certainly wasn't greater than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the intensity of the firing from this heavy artillery which you say was landing in the entire area, including the centre of Fakovici, what was the intensity?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the time shells were being fired every minute of the time. It was no longer possible to keep track of all the shells falling or to keep count or where they were falling. Those were a series, if you like, of shells being fired from Bacevci and Bacevacko Polje, and there was additional firing coming from semi-automatic rifles and other infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And at this time were there Muslim civilians in Fakovici that you could see?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment, one moment. Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. Your Honours, the witness said there was additional firing coming from automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, PAMs, and infantry weapons. So the PAMs were not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did mention PAMs, in other words, as well, apart from semi-automatic rifles and infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you confirmed there were Muslim civilians in Fakovici, how many again roughly -- if you can roughly estimate how many were there at that time.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in Fakovici myself, but according to what people who had arrived from that area said there were thousands and hundreds of civilians there or that's at least what the people said who had reached Zanjevski Potok. They said there was an enormous number of civilians in the area and that many people had been killed in Fakovici as a result of the shelling from Bacevci. It was literally impossible to see anything because of the amount of dust in the air in the Fakovici area. You couldn't see what was going on on account of the dust. So many shells had landed in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us you were in Zanjevski Potok in this period?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that that's part of Fakovici. Can you explain what you mean when you say "I wasn't in Fakovici myself."

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area in which I happened to be, Zanjevski Potok, is about one and a half or two kilometres from Fakovici; that was the distance thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From the centre of Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know how many Muslims were killed from the shelling on the 5th of October, 1992, in the Fakovici-Zanjevo area?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, could I just ask for Defence counsel for the sake of clarity now that the witness has been able to use the map to say where certain places where, if he could just establish where he was so that we would be able to follow his testimony more carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think yesterday when he mentioned Zanjevo Potok he didn't mark it on the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I'll ask the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if it was there, I mean, I wouldn't imagine that this is the size of Detroit or London. I mean, we're talking of very small places.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps I can ask the witness to indicate, initially at least how close --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Indicate the closest you got to Fakovici on the 5th of October, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's a very good question. Yes. Because the -- Ms. Sellers and Mr. Jones, the X which you see at 35 minutes to the south of Fakovici is, I think, the Zanjevo Potok that he mentioned yesterday, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, if you can indicate where you --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you've just circled an area to the right of Fakovici. Is it correct, then, you were also in that area on the 5th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you mark -- answer the question first. Answer the question first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And now where you marked, put that oval mark on the map, could you put AI next to it, please. That means Alic, Ibro, your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And one question which might clarify this. In your language, Potok is a small creek or stream, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's obviously difficult to interpret that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What does -- "Rijeka" means a river. Do you agree to that? In your language "Rijeka" means a river, doesn't it? What's happening? What's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't speak English, I'm sorry. There's a difference in our language between a river on the one hand and a stream on the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. What is a Potok? What is a Potok? Could you describe how it is different from a Rijeka, and we get there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. A Potok is a very small place where water runs, very small. And a river is a bigger thing. When you have several Potoks coming together, what you get as a result is a river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So that clears it. He is agreeing that Potok for all intents and purposes is a stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so the Zanjevo stream, Zanjevski Potok, can you indicate on the map where it runs.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did mark it, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, the flow of the stream.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zanjevski Potok runs right here, this side, near Zanjevo itself and it mouths --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think you said "the mouth of the Drina." It wasn't interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so perhaps now you can help with this: The X which is marked just below Fakovici which you marked yesterday, what site is that? What does that represent? If you put your pen on the map I'll direct you. If you point to Fakovici -- Fakovici, where it says "Fakovici." Yes, now go down to the X without marking anything, please. The other direction, the X. Yes. That X, what does that represent, that X?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This X represents a place from which you could observe Fakovici. It's called Stijena, or rock, as I said yesterday. We travelled this area on our way from Fakovici when we went to school or the other way around from Bratunac back to Fakovici. This was a footpath.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yeah, I hope everything is clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I mean, let's proceed because at the end of the day this is of relative importance. But anyway let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course feel free to put any further question on this, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, it's simply obviously to establish from where he was observing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm not sure if you answered the question of how many Muslims died from shelling, shooting, that day, on the 5th of October, 1992, in Fakovici and Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an exact figure, but what I heard from other people was between 50 and 100. At least what I was told from those people at Fakovici. I did see a number of people myself at Radijevici Potok, or rather, Zanjevski Potok. People had been killed. It was impossible to reach every single place in order to check how many people had been killed. Shells were falling all over, over the forest, over the fields, over the houses, and at the centre of Fakovici itself. Therefore, it was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I think you told us that shelling started from the Serbian side around 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. Before that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether the witness has mentioned a time period. That would be helpful, if you can just confirm that. He just said shelling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't remember, I don't recollect either, having heard that. Perhaps Mr. Jones could --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He did. I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't bother about finding it. Just put the question again and he'll confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall when the firing from artillery from Serbia started?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said that. Probably it wasn't interpreted. It was between 3.00 and 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before that time, before that shelling started, did you see any houses either being set on fire or which were on fire?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any smoke at Fakovici. I saw nothing burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, were you aware that day or not of whether there were any airplanes in the air?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At one point in time - it's very difficult for me to specify when because the explosion was so powerful and the shelling was so intense - there was a plane that arrived from the Bratunac area, a field plane as we called it. Just over Fakovici, some sort of a boiler was dropped from the plane which landed somewhere in Fakovici, I can't say where exactly, and exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you tell us what a boiler is, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A boiler, that's at least what I believed, was a water boiler from the sort you have in a bathroom that you use to heat water to run a bath. And people told us that the same kind of water boilers were dropped on other areas, too, and those were sometimes filled with explosives. Screws and bolts, bits of iron, scraps, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And how destructive are those bombs?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't near enough to see how destructive they were, but the explosion certainly resounded very far. And bits were flying all over the place. That's at least what the people who actually were there said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. When you say "the people who actually were there," were where?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people were right in the middle of Fakovici. There were many people there from Zanjevo. There was some people from my village who were there to get food, civilians, who were there in order to find food. There were people from Visegrad, from Zepa, from those other areas. The people who came to Jagodnja the next day and told the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you have any knowledge of how many Serb soldiers were in Fakovici on the 5th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, there were supposed to have been between 2 and 300 people in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Two clarifications, firstly it's the 5th of October, 1992, just for the transcript. When you say 2 to 300 people, are you talking about civilians in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What are you talking about then?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About soldiers, Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you hear whether any weapons or ammunition were recovered in Fakovici on the 5th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was a small amount, a medium amount, a large amount?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the people who had been down there and what they said, apparently there was a great deal of weapons and ammunition there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know where they were found, what locations these weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also heard that that ammunition was found at the old school and also at the playground in front of the old school. I think there was a kind of transport vehicle, a kind of truck or something like that. It was yellow and it was found there. I don't really remember what exactly it was, but it was a kind of transport vehicle. And it was found in front of that old school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know if any weapons or ammunition were found in houses in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was told that ammunition and weapons were found in every single house at Fakovici and that even some medical equipment was found there, single-use medical kit or whatever, things that could have been used to tend the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, you mentioned a vehicle, a kind of truck, which was yellow. Now, in your language was the word "Zuti" --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We may have the same problem in a moment. But is it right that "Zuti" means yellow in Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean does yellow mean yellow? Of course it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I can think of a better way of asking that question, but I think we got there. Does Moja Zuca, does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I can only tell you that I have a son who is blond, and I call him Moja Zuca, my blondie, kind of thing. It's a kind of language I might use when talking to a child, baby talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness had said "yellow" and the translation is blond, which is not exactly the same. Did you mean blond in terms of blond hair or in terms of yellow hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yellow, except that it's not used in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I think we got there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want to show the witness D135, please, Defence Exhibit 135.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'll direct your attention to the third paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just ask a question, please? I seem to have a problem with my headset because I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and that is a problem that we need to look into straight away. Are you receiving interpretation of what I am saying now? Are you hearing anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you are receiving interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's start from this. Usher, usher, could you please change his -- give him a new one or another one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it seems to be all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I mean, it's -- Mr. Alic, if at any time it recurs, if you have the same problem again, do like you did this time, tell me immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I would ask you, Mr. Alic, to read just to yourself, firstly, the third paragraph of this page. It's not necessary for you to read the whole thing, just the third paragraph for context. And let me know when you've finished.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm finished, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's just that last sentence which I want to ask you about. And I'll read it in Bosnian, where it says: [B/C/S spoken] [Interpretation] "At the time when they were walking down the Drina, our weapons were not being used anymore" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And unfortunately the interpreters had not quite understood what has just been read.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. In fact, the purpose of the exercise was for the witness to hear B/C/S being spoken rather than to have translation, although I appreciate that that's important. We do have an exhibit with the English translation, otherwise I can just read the sentence again slowly and then we all know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try again in my best B/C/S. [B/C/S spoken] [Interpretation] "At the moment when they were walking down the Drina, our weapons died down and my Zuca was still being used."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, my question is: You've said how you've call your son Moja Zuca, meaning my blondie or my yellow one. Do you agree that Moja Zuca can mean my yellow one or my blond one?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in the context of this paragraph which you've just read, do you -- do you have any idea of what Moja Zuca might refer to and also in light of what you've told us about Fakovici on the 5th of October, 1992, and what was recovered there?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to my opinion, this could have been the vehicle that was yellow, and I don't know whether it had a PAM or a machine-gun mounted on it. I don't know. So that vehicle at any rate was yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd like to show the Defence -- sorry, the witness a different exhibit now. I think it's P257. Yes, P257. And for the record, this is Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior Sarajevo CSB, security services centre, SNB, national security service sector, Sarajevo. It's dated 15th October, 1992, and I'm going to read in fact the first two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: "Subject: Information acquired by the SNB on the attack on enemy forces on villages in the Skelani and Bratunac sector. Through intelligence work, we have obtained a lot of security-related information about the enemy attack on the villages of Fakovici, Kutijesi, Boljevici, and Radijevici in the area of Skelani and Bratunac. In this way, we were informed that the attack against these villages started simultaneously 5 October 1992 at 1200 hours and lasted until 1600 hours. A total of 22 members of the Serbian army were killed while the enemy had around 40 dead. On this occasion, the enemy burnt down several family houses and the old school in Fakovici and took away a three-barrel M-55, 20-millimetre, anti-aircraft gun, and a four-barrel gun, three 82-millimetre MB mortar, one of which was not working; three or four Zoljas, 64-millimetre, M-80 hand-held rocket launcher; one M-84 PM light machine-gun; ten AP, automatic rifle; a number of hand-grenades, and 1.500 7.62-millimetre bullets. And according to another source, in addition to the above-stated, two tractors of ammunition." Now, first I want to ask you about the school, the old school which is mentioned there. Now, you told us earlier that as far -- well, if you could repeat your evidence so I don't have to refer to the transcript. What did you know about what was actually recovered in the school in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ammunition was found at that school and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you also told us yesterday about seeing soldiers as early as I believe it was April or May outside the school in Fakovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know what that school was being used for?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably for the training of the soldiers of the Serb army. It was an old school which had a big hole, and there was another smaller room on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And there's this reference to three-barrel gun and a four-barrel gun. You mentioned a gun which was mounted on a yellow vehicle. Do you know which of those guns it was? If not, it doesn't matter, but if you can help.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the knowledge of those people who told me that, roughly speaking, it could have been a PAM.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which is an anti-aircraft gun. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this report by the Serbs says that the enemy burnt down several family houses, several. Now, first of all, I want to be clear, your evidence -- you've told us you didn't see any houses burned before the Serb artillery attack from the other side of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated the 15th of October, 1992. Are you aware whether or not civilians went into Fakovici in the days following the 5th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Civilians went looking for food on a daily basis, so they did go in. And some of them even brought winter frames from Fakovici and everything else they needed because our village had been burned down and they even took stuff to other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Before moving on to another document, it refers further down to -- it says: "According to the sources, two black men were seen in these formations, enemy formations." In 1992, did you ever see or hear of black men on the Muslim side in our area?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I saw a black man for the first time in Srebrenica in 1993 when the UNPROFOR people came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would it have been a common or uncommon sight, black men in the Drina valley in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I'd never seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, just sticking with this reference to several houses, and I want you to bear that in mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want to show the witness a new exhibit which doesn't have an ERN. We can distribute copies. Sorry, with the usher's assistance. And this is the 1991 census for Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sarajevo, May 1991. I want to ask the witness first to look for Jagodnja and Joseva. It says "50 households in Jagodnja and 40 in Joseva."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is that about right? Is that about accurate?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And for Fakovici we see 54 households and 67 flats. Does that seem about right to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So according to the document we just saw, several houses were burnt out of these 54 households and 67 flats? That's right. That's more of an observation from the document. I'll move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I have an exhibit number for that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I've understood Defence counsel correctly, then his commentary on that is not a question that's put to the witness as a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's put the question to the witness already basically by reference to the document, and the witness said -- he acknowledged the number of houses and flats shown in this document is correct and then the rest of the question by Mr. Jones, if you can call it a question, does not elicit an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was axiomatic, so I withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. So I think we can leave it at that. We do not have a statement from the accused on that. This will be -- will become Defence Exhibit D829.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I may be wrong but I think the witness might be a little tired. Perhaps we can ask him. He was looking like he might be tired. We could just have a break earlier if he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can have the break now. Now, incidentally while we are at this, I've been informed that there is a possibility of moving tomorrow's sitting from the afternoon to the morning. From our side, of course myself and Judge Brydensholt are quite agreeable to this. On the part of Judge Eser, unfortunately there was or there is a prior engagement that he definitely has to attend to, which will keep him tied until 10.00 in the morning, let's say 10.00, and then we will be flexible between 10.00 and 10.15 or 10.30, whatever. My suggestion is the following, and please do come back to us after the break. I have these options to propose. That we start at 10.00 -- when I say "10.00," it could be 10.15, as soon as Judge Eser finishes with what he will be doing tomorrow morning. We could start at 10.00, we could start at 10.00, break at 11.30, resume at 12.00, break at 1.30, resume at 2.00 and finish definitively at 2.45. That's one option which would give us the entire three hours and 45 minutes. Alternatively, we could start at 10.00 right through until 11.45, then one break, starting again 12.15 right through to 2.00, and that would give us three hours and 30 minutes. I'm leaving all options open. If you prefer not to change anything and stick to the afternoon schedule that we have, then of course I will direct that we sit in the afternoon as scheduled.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I can say immediately that we're happy with any proposal from the Bench. We're entirely in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then the Prosecution, I know you have this problem of Mr. Di Fazio trying to dig deep into the four million document archives to locate any missing document that Mr. Jones is anxiously waiting for, but we can still I think meet -- sit at 10.00 in the morning. But of course we want to make sure that arrangements can be made to have interpreters here in the morning plus the court recorders and everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're entirely in your hands also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. But I need a response from the rest of the technical staff, interpreters and recorders and everything. All right? So we'll have a -- you think you will be okay if we give you a 30-minute break, Mr. Alic? If you are too tired to continue, we can call it a day and you can come back tomorrow and we will continue tomorrow if you are too tired. If you think you'll be feeling better after 30 minutes, then we will try to sit for, say, another hour and then you can go back to your hotel. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I can continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now. And then after that we'll play it by the ear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I see Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With a view of the scheduling of tomorrow, the Prosecution is pleased to start as well 10.00 or 10.15 as you like. But we have requested the Trial Chamber with a view to the preparation by the submission of my counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, we would prefer to enable him to start his submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the end --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And for that purpose, you should be informed that he might need around a quarter of an hour, 15 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Is that all right with you, Mr. Jones? I suppose you shouldn't have any problems with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. And if you would notify us if he intends to rely on authority so we can prepare for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I suppose Mr. Wubben will pass on the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So the decision is that tomorrow we'll start at 10.00 -- could be a few minutes later. We'll start immediately when Judge Eser finishes with the other work that he is dealing with which will be first opportunity after 10.00. Thanks. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will continue. We have more or less three quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any time you notice that your client is -- sorry, your witness is tired, please tell us and we'll stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I'll keep a clean lookout. And to make progress, I'll start immediately with the next exhibit, which is D735, please. If the witness could be shown that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I'm returning to the subject of Djoko Djokic, and I'll just remind you of your testimony that you're aware of a tradition where a unit is renamed after the fallen commander. Now, this is entitled "TO Skelani" -- well, at the top it's written "TO Skelani, list of fighters Djoko Djokic unit, Fakovici." The date is October 29, 1992. List of fighters of Djoko Djokic unit, Fakovici, who received monetary allowance for children. And it's signed by detachment commander Vukoman Simic October 30, 1992. Do you know Vukoman Simic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Vukoman Simic, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village of Popovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And we see at number 1, Djoko Djokic, and then in brackets Ivana. Do you know who Ivana is?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivana is Djoko Djokic's daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, actually if the witness can be shown D739 quickly at this point and we'll keep the other exhibit for the moment. Just for the record, this is minutes prepared by the military police and Vukoman Simic on handover of objects confiscated from citizens from the area of Fakovici that were collected from Muslim houses and facilities. And then at the bottom we see "received by Vukoman Simic."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know of any other Vukoman Simics in the Fakovici area?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukoman Simic is from Popovici. He's about 40, and I know he used to work at Zvornik at a construction company.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is Popovici close to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, in fact, I am finished with both D735 and D739. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could the witness now please be shown D734. And just to explain the dates and the title, it's the list of soldiers who received salaries for August and half of September in Radijevici. It's signed in November 1992, so evidently retroactive payment for August and half of September 1992. If we turn to the last page, we see Djoko Djokic unit -- sorry, it's the last page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you see that -- now, last page in Bosnian as well obviously. You see signature Djoko Djokic, unit Fakovici, November 25, 1992, detachment commander, Vukoman Simic, and it's signed that the above-mentioned soldiers received salaries for August and half of September. Now, that's just by way of background. I'm going to ask you about some of the entries in this document. Firstly, can you go to number 50, Radusa Jovanovic, and this is on the list of soldiers. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And could you tell us where he's from?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radusa Jovanovic is from Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Do you know Andrija Markovic, a number 52?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrija Markovic is the son of Beli from Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go to number 67 you see the name of Bola Bozic [phoen], and it says his salary was given to Nikolic, Ljubo, Top. Is that name familiar to you, Bola Bozic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bolo -- or rather, Bola, as it says here, and Bozic as well, it's a man from Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. It says that his salary was given to Nikolic, Ljubo, Top. I want you to bear that name in mind for a bit. We're going to come back to it. At number 71, and that's 71 on that same column, it says that Novica Savic's salary was given to Vidoje Maksimovic. Do you know Vidoje Maksimovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is he the person you referred to yesterday in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The person who said that Muslims had to move 40 kilometres from the Drina, that conversation?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you later hear of what rank he achieved, what became of him in the military?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's okay. And now if we look at item 86, and I think that's maybe only in the Bosnian because we didn't include all the names in English. We see the name Nedjo Nikolic. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedjo Nikolic is from Fakovici and he attended primary school with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've finished with that exhibit for the time being. And now we have a new exhibit and the ERN is 04359977. And it says in English "Fighters' payroll, Djoko Djokic Company, 3rd Platoon, Orlica, Tegare."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll wait until you have the document. Now, first I asked you yesterday about how -- when you told us about how Muslims were ethnically cleansed or expelled from their villages in Tegare and Orlica in May 1992. Are you aware whether that was done by local Serbs or by Serbs from outside the area?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the accounts of people who had been chased away from their houses, it was perpetrated by locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And we see that this is -- this refers to the Djoko Djokic Company, which we saw is in Fakovici, and this is apparently the 3rd Platoon, Orlica, Tegare. Were you aware that Serbs from Orlica and Tegare were in Fakovici units?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before the war, were those areas, Orlica and Tegare, linked to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that Serbs had some kind of exercises in Fakovici. You said that they had shooting exercises above Grabovacka Rijeka and you referred to a creek called Ruljevici. Do you know whether Serbs from areas such as Orlica and Tegare went to such training? Did you hear that information?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the knowledge of people who came from Bratunac at that period of time in 1992, for as long as there was free movement, people used to tell me that they used to see people from Tegare in Fakovici, in that area. And they were uniformed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we just clarify the interpretation once again. The witness has said "according to the knowledge of people who came from Bratunac." I don't see that it's clear in the transcript. Could the witness clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, but I don't want to contradict you, Ms. Vidovic, in the least. But I think it's line -- page 81, line 2 says precisely that. "A. According to the knowledge of people who came from Bratunac." And you want to say it in which way?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the knowledge of people from Bratunac; that's what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what it says. I mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine for my purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can we proceed? I think that's what it says, actually, in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or else I'm not understanding. I mean, either of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We can raise it again tomorrow, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We see number 15 of that list, Nedjo Nikolic, who was at 86 of the document we just saw, and you've confirmed that you know him. Roughly what age was he, to your knowledge? When was he born?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedjo Nikolic used to go to school with me. And according to my knowledge, he -- I think he was born in 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll ask for an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, Mr. Jones, will become Defence Exhibit D830.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have another document -- we're obviously going to proceed with some documents in this session. The next one is again a new document. The ERN is 04359973. And in the meantime, for the record, I'll read what it states. "Skelani TO, Territorial Defence, Djoko Djokic unit, Fakovici. LD, personal income for the volunteers for August 1992. Number 1, Slobodan Misic, signature, 20.000; second, Ljubo Nikolic, signature, 20.000; paid in Radijevici on 31 October 1992." Then we see company officer Vukoman Simic and then a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So firstly, Witness, would you confirm this, at least on the face of it, refers to Djoko Djokic unit, Fakovici, as part of Skelani TO?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this is payment to volunteers for August 1992, and it's signed by Vukoman Simic, who you've told us about. What would you understand by the term "volunteers"?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Volunteers were people who used to come from Serbia to Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you aware that that was occurring, that volunteers would come from Serbia to Fakovici in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, when our people --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt the witness but I'm going to ask that we go into closed session because I -- based on the proofing, I believe there might be something which he will say which should be in closed session. It's for the witness's own benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection on the Prosecution's part?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session -- private session is enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I merely want to draw attention to the record for the two names, Ljubo Nikolic, which we saw at D734 at number 67, and Slobodan Misic whose name will be familiar to us, I trust, already. Sorry, may I have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I once again would like to ask Defence was he asking a question or making a comment or was this -- the question about the two names, I don't know whether you're resuming a point, whether you're asking a question. I would just like that to be clarified because I want to be able to distinguish between Mr. Alic's testimony and commentary on the documents or the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's not commentary. It's really for the benefit of the Chamber that those names be borne in mind as we look at subsequent documents and also in light of submissions which have been made. It's not a question for the witness. It's so that we can all follow the significance of names which have been mentioned, and I trust that's not objectionable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as an explanation, I take it it's a reminder or the beginning of argument. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document with ERN number 04359973, two pages, one in B/C/S and one in English, in the corresponding translation thereof, is being marked as Defence Exhibit D831.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. And we move to a new exhibit and it's the one which -- has already been distributed, so we don't have more copies to distribute. And it's 01297984 to 01297987. And for the record, first page it says "Peace Bridge Danube, Odgovor, Belgrade, Bumerang, Osijek." Next page, "Dogs of war, Slobodan Misic, TOP, how I killed Croats and Muslims." I'm going to read a section, parts of the first section, and then ask you some questions, Mr. Alic. It says: "Testimony of a killer." And, actually, just for Your Honours' benefit, I should say that the B/C/S -- in the B/C/S version there is a lead-in which was difficult to interpret -- difficult to translate, and that's why we have three dots indicating that there's a section which we're still having trouble translating. For our purposes, we've translated what's relevant for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So the section I'm reading goes as follows: "Things started -- already started cooking in Bosnia. I was looking for a way to go there." And if you see that, Mr. Alic, it's on the page which is 01297987, and it says at the top [B/C/S spoken]. And then you'll see in the first column the words [B/C/S spoken]. Do you see that section? It's the -- if you see [B/C/S spoken], then you see two paragraphs, then on the left-hand column you'll see [B/C/S spoken]. Then the question [B/C/S spoken]. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Usher, where are you? You need to -- come, I show you, please. You need to put this and focus on this part here, this paragraph here. All right. Take it and bring it back afterwards. Put it on the ELMO so that others can follow, too. And if we could zoom in the first -- very first paragraph just at the left-hand side -- yes, that's enough. That's enough. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you see on the screen now in front of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The very first paragraph below that -- beneath that bold line over there at the top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I'm going to read some parts of that from that paragraph. "Things already started cooking in Bosnia. I was looking for a way to go there. Why? Didn't you have enough war and killing? Volunteer from here, from Vranje, had some connection with Skelani. Few of us took off with him and we went to Uzice and then to Bajina Basta and then across Drina to Bratunac. We reported to the Territorial Defence there and they deployed us in Fakovici." I skip the next question. "What was actually your task? "15 of us, volunteers from Vranje and the surrounding area" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Push it down now. Usher, you have to push it down, please. Skip the next -- more, more. Yes. Perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: "What was actually your task? "15 of us, volunteers from Vranje and the surrounding area, were stationed in Fakovici. We undertook actions from there with local inhabitants who used to come from Bratunac. Muslim villages were up in the hills and we cleansed them one by one." Now, do you agree, firstly, this is referring to a volunteer from Serbia, as you've described?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that he was, according to this, deployed in Fakovici by the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And he says how he went there when things had started cooking in Bosnia. I believe that's an expression in your language. Would that refer to the start of the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. When it says here "things already started cooking in Bosnia," that's the section after -- he refers to coming back from Vukovar, would that refer in your language to when things started in Bosnia, the war started?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, when things heated up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And of course we've just seen the name of Slobodan Misic in the previous exhibit. You've seen the name Slobodan Misic at the start of this article, have you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the way, perhaps we could clear this up. Has he seen this document before or is it the first time that he's seeing the document now?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll allow the witness to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, of course. I didn't ask the question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. No indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was that in our offices here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Is that where you saw it, here in The Hague, in our offices?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So he knows -- because otherwise I was going to tell him, give him time to read the article or the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That would spare us having to go through it bit by bit. But of course go ahead with all the questions that you have in regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in this interview the person refers to being stationed in Fakovici and from there cleansing Muslim villages up in the hills. Now, Joseva and Jagodnja are up in the hills above Fakovici. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And those villages were attacked and people were killed in May 1992 by Serb soldiers coming from the direction of Fakovici. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And who were receiving orders, as you told us, from Slavko Jovanovic and Djoko Djokic, both of whom are from Fakovici. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we've seen in documents and do you confirm that those units and those troops were part of Skelani TO?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
