utterances.text: Moving on to a second section. "You say that you undertook actions. What do you mean by that? "When we undertook actions, all volunteers that were accommodated in Serb villages gathered there. Special units came from Bratunac consisting of people from this area who knew the terrain. The task of these people was to disable Muslim guards around the villages before the attack. During that time, we surrounded them and started attacks at dawn. We burned everything that was in our path, threw bombs into houses, fired. We captured a number of Muslims and sent them to Bratunac. After our actions, villages were completely destroyed, Zanjevo, Tegare, and seven or eight other villages. According to my assessment, 4.000 to 5.000 Muslims were killed. More than 1.000 people were killed in the forest in the village of Tegare in three to four hours only." My question is: Does that correspond firstly to what you experienced in Jagodnja and Joseva, this description?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Does it correspond to what you heard from refugees from Zanjevo and Tegare?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And does it correspond to what you heard and what you were told by the person who you mentioned in private session a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That they were volunteers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And now the next section the question is: "Who did you fight against? Against Muslims" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I'll direct the usher a little bit. Yes, and when I give you a sign, then please move to the next column at the top. All right. Thank you. We are here [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well-spoken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It says there: "Who did you fight against? Against Muslim army? "No, they were civilians, villagers, in most cases insufficiently armed with double-barrelled guns and similar rifles." Now, that's the opinion of a Serb, a volunteer from Serbia who we've seen was in the Djoko Djokic unit in Fakovici, that it was not a Muslim army. Do you agree or disagree with that opinion?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I do think that as Defence counsel is going through this document he is adding things, like he says there was not a Muslim army. It seems as if he is saying that he fought against civilians. Now what is not clearly on the document, I think that certainly should be put to the witness. What is not clearly written on the document, let's not put that to the witness unless it's in the context of a separate question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge, can I borrow yours because I don't have the English translation now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I must admit I don't see the difference, frankly, that it was not a Muslim army that they were fighting against.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. This is why I wanted the translation word for word. The question put to the interviewee, Ms. Sellers, the question put by the interviewer to Misic is: "Who did you fight against? Against a Muslim army?" And the answer is: "No, they were civilians, villagers, in most cases insufficiently armed with double-barrelled guns and similar rifles." It is true that this does not mean that the interviewed person, Misic, is saying that a Muslim army did not exist. He is saying that on that particular occasion they did not fight a Muslim army or a military formation but they only fought civilians. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the occasion, though, which you're referring to, Your Honour. In the previous paragraph he refers to Zanjevo, Tegare, and several other villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This -- throughout all this activity that is mentioned. When I say "this occasion," I mean when they supposedly destroyed all these villages, attacked here and attacked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All these activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what I want to ensure is that this is not taken as a suggestion to the witness that the Misic, Slobodan Misic, is categorically stating that there was no such thing at the time in Bosnia as a Muslim army, because he's not saying that. He is just saying "we did not fight against an army."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. And I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise, I mean, because I read you well --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I understood it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: In 1992, Mr. Alic, in your area, was there a Muslim army, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, further down Misic says: "We did kill women." "We did kill women." It's on 01297986. Now you've, confirmed that Muslim women were killed by Serb soldiers coming from the direction of Fakovici, and you've said that they were apparently receiving orders. Now were those people who attacked you -- I'm sorry, I think I have to consult with my colleague. She's drawing my attention to something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You have to go to the third column. No, that's the third column, the second column. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's simply actually a confirmation that indeed in Joseva Muslim women were killed by Serb soldiers coming from the direction of Fakovici who appeared to be receiving orders from Slavko Jovanovic and Djoko Djokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't see you stand up, Ms. Sellers --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to look at the transcript first and say is that a question that we're now asking Mr. Alic to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it's a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It wasn't clear by the transcript what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise to the interpreters. I forgot my microphone -- to switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alic, can you confirm that indeed in Joseva Muslim women were killed by Serb soldiers coming from the direction of Fakovici who appeared to be receiving orders from Slavko Jovanovic and Djoko Djokic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now moving on to the next section. "Why didn't you capture them?" I don't know if we have that on the monitor. Yes, thank you very much. "We captured some of them. Here is what happened to me." "Why didn't you capture them? We captured some of them. Here is what happened to me. One morning I captured two Muslims. They watched the village, and I approached them behind their back. I took them to the municipality. We questioned them there and then we took them to Bratunac and there they asked what are we going to do with them. What do you mean what are you going to do? Give them to me. I took them to a bridge, killed them, and pushed them into the Drina. Were you or some of your co-fighters punished for killing prisoners? Who would punish you? You could kill as many as you liked. Nobody would tell anything." My question is: Does that correspond to your experience in this area and at this time that Serbs did indeed kill men and women with impunity?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time the daily trips from Jagodnja and Joseva, the people who took the road to Zanjevo and wherever they could go, there were cases of people leaving and never returning. There were countless such cases people leaving the area, never to return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he hasn't answered the second part of the question, and I don't know if he is really in a position to answer that. The question by Mr. Jones was: Whether you are aware that the Serbs committed all this killing and got away scot-free, that they were never punished for it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have never heard of a single case where a Serb was punished because he had killed Muslims who went about in search of food or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Back to you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Have you ever heard whether Slobodan Misic has been punished, either from Yugoslavia or at this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not something that I've heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Going on to the next paragraph: "What happened between those actions, as you call them? "Mostly nothing. We hung around the village, conducted reconnaissance, set ambushes for Muslims who usually came down from the hills on horses at night trying to get some food. They broke off stalks from grains and made bread from them or they just chewed wheat. They did not choose. They also ate pigs who had escaped to the forest. There was an enormous hunger in Muslim villages, and they had to risk their lives or starve to death. We used to wait for them in the ambush and kill them when they returned. On one occasion, I captured some man, Alija from Zanjevo, who is known for his crimes against Serbs. He was young, 35 to 36 years old. I captured him above Fakovici while he was in reconnaissance. I asked him, Balija, where shall we go now? And he told me, Chetnik, don't kill me. Nope, I said, I won't. I riddled him with shots and decapitated him." Now, there's a reference there to someone above Fakovici doing reconnaissance. Is that something which people, including refugees from your village, did, conducted reconnaissance above Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our people did go to that area above Fakovici, like I said before, Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did some or many of them not come back?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who would go in search of food, especially in search of food, there were many of those people who never returned. And we don't know what became of them. They came from all over the place, Visegrad, to Gradac, Zepa, from the surroundings of Srebrenica, and it simply wasn't possible to keep all those people under control to know where they were or where they were going. There were cases where we stopped people from moving in that particular direction going through the fields because people had been known to be killed there. We explained this to them. They said, We have to go. It's either we die down there or we starve to death together with our children. It was a dreadful situation and no one dared tell anyone else not to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And then here the last paragraph I'm going to read where it says: "What is the total number of people you killed in this war? "I killed some 70 to 80 people. I do not know precisely." Now, my question is: Do you know roughly how many people died in 1992 in Jagodnja and Joseva, Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, I can tell you about that if you like. Within that period of time, until March 1993, the total was 46 or 47 persons, including women and children. I'm talking about those two villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And those are -- that's not including refugees. That's just inhabitants of Jagodnja and Joseva. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just the inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So 46 or 47 persons out of those two villages were killed in that period?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, that's the point I was waiting -- first counsel asked how many people died and now we're saying how many people were killed. And Mr. Alic might be able to tell us, is he talking about persons killed within this context or persons who died because we've mentioned women and children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. I think you can clear that up --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Out of the inhabitants, the original inhabitants of Jagodnja and Joseva, how many died violent deaths, I'll put it that way, in 1992 and up to March 1993?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered that question. 46 or 47, I can't be certain. Perhaps more, perhaps less, but thereabouts. These people were killed by a bullet, by a shell, somebody who tripped over a mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think we can -- well, I would ask for an exhibit number for this document and also for the other one which was distributed with it. I'll cover that tomorrow, but it's probably convenient to assign it an exhibit number now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Let me have it back. And this will be 832, D832. Let me describe it. This document consists of four pages in B/C/S starting with ERN 01297984 right through and inclusive of 01297987.
